name: Bread & Butter
summary: Lead-intelligence platform with server-side tracking: it captures the full visitor journey from the first visit, then enriches, scores and nurtures the moment someone submits an email, using verified identities instead of IP-based company guesses.
best_for: marketing and revenue teams that want engaged visitors (people who filled a form or left an email) automatically enriched, scored and nurtured, on a usable freemium tier
skip_if: you want IP-based company guessing at anonymous visitors: that’s a different tool class (Leadfeeder-style) with a different accuracy and compliance profile, or you run many small sites, where per-website pricing adds up
honest_knock: Two meters to watch: it prices per WEBSITE (multi-site setups multiply the $49) and the AI features run on compute-credit blocks that stack as usage grows. On privacy, refined twice in open dialogue with the vendor (16 Jul 2026, verified against their docs). The anonymous journey IS tracked from the first visit, server-side via their site plugin. So ad-blockers and Safari’s ITP don’t strip it the way they kill client-side scripts: the vendor estimates 30-50% of high-value traffic is lost to client-side blocking. What stays dormant until someone submits an email is identity resolution: the ‘hand-raise’ that connects the captured history to a verified person. You still owe normal GDPR care on enriched data, and the real trade-off is simply this: no IP-based guessing at which company an anonymous visitor works for.

pricing.entry_price_terms: a month per website (5,000 lead profiles)
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-11-26 on breadbutter.io/pricing and the help article 'How do Credits work', support.breadbutter.io/article/201) Three published plans and a custom Enterprise tier. Free at $0: unlimited website traffic, one domain, 200 stored lead profiles, 30 days of attribution retention, no credits, your existing web forms, lead capture and content gates, social logins with your own branding, visitor journey tracking, list export to CSV, Google Sheets and Mailchimp, a Slack post when a lead converts, unlimited team members, one-day email response. AI Enabled Pro at $49 a month per website: one domain plus 3 subdomains, 5,000 lead profiles, 5 years of attribution retention, 3,000 credits a month, one-hour email response, plus attribution reporting, journey and event tracking, custom views, real-time email verification, Focused Score, profile enrichment, Nurture AI messages, the Focused Index and Ratio, the Intelligence Brief in Slack and in Salesforce, HubSpot or Pipedrive, and Zapier and webhooks. AI assistant Pro Plus at $199 a month per website: one domain plus 9 subdomains, 10,000 lead profiles, lifetime retention, 10,000 credits a month, plus AI assistant reports in Claude or ChatGPT, Lookalikes, Lead Gen Autopilot and an MCP server. Enterprise is priced around your websites and volume ('Let's talk', for larger teams and agencies) and adds several websites under one account, a data warehouse, the Intelligence Stream and onboarding with their team. Extra credits: 10,000 for $89 a month on Pro and Pro Plus; the help article adds that pricing can vary by plan and by partner and that the current price is shown in the app. What credits pay for, per that article: 2 credits a month for each stored profile beyond the plan allowance, 3 credits per Intelligence Brief generated, on average 25 to 250 credits per profile researched, a quarter of a credit per AI assistant question plus 1 credit per 100 rows (Pro Plus), and 100 credits per lookalike plus its research. Unused credits do not carry over, and Free cannot add credits. Two points on the same day disagree: the help article gives Free 500 stored profiles where the pricing table says 200, and it calls the Intelligence Stream part of an Enterprise license while the pricing table lists it in the Zapier and webhook rows of Pro and Pro Plus. Pro has a 30-day trial and no credit card is asked. The pricing page publishes no annual rate.

compare_with.name: Leadfeeder
compare_with.why: Leadfeeder guesses the company behind anonymous IPs: useful when it lands, though remote work and VPNs often return an ISP instead; Bread & Butter tracks behaviour server-side from the first visit and resolves identity when a visitor hands over an email. Pick by what your sales team acts on: company guesses or verified people
